overall: The AG resolved the complaints by informal action and found no violation: both meetings were canceled before convening, so the posting rules were not triggered, and the March 28 cancellation was not regulated. A reminder about recording posting date and time was issued.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notice for the March 27 meeting was not posted at least 48 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law's notice posting procedures are not implicated when a meeting does not go forward.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 27 meeting notice failed to conspicuously record the date and time it was posted.
allegations.key_passage: Although we find no violation, we remind the Committee of the requirement to conspicuously record the date and time that a meeting notice is posted, rather than received, by the town clerk.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 28 meeting cancellation notice failed to conspicuously record the date and time it was posted.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not impose any requirements on the cancellation of a meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
